ig_caption:
Stuck around 1200? It's rarely the opening.

Many games at this level are decided by a piece left hanging or a threat nobody saw. Five habits that help: check every check, capture and threat; ask what your opponent's last move wants; review your losses; play slower games; and stop after two losses in a row.

Which one will you try in your next game? 👇

#chess #chessimprovement #learnchess #chesstips #chessrating #plateau #chessjourney
alt: Slide 1: Cover. Stuck at 1200? Five habits that unstick you. No new openings required.
Slide 2: Habit 1. Before every move, look at checks, captures and threats, for both sides.
Slide 3: Habit 2. Ask what your opponent's last move wants before making your own plan.
Slide 4: Habit 3. Review your losses. Find the one move where the game turned.
Slide 5: Habit 4. Play slower games, such as 15 minutes plus 10 seconds, so you have time to use the habits.
Slide 6: Habit 5. Stop after two losses in a row, because the next game is often played angry and fast.
Slide 7: A Chess Journey poster. Every plateau is a line on the poster, and so is the climb after it.

slides.title: Checks, captures, threats
slides.body: Many games at this level end with a piece left hanging or a threat nobody saw. Before you move, list every check, capture and threat on the board.
slides.note: Do it for your opponent too. Then play your move.

slides.title: Ask what their move wants
slides.body: Every move does something: attacks a piece, opens a line, prepares a check. Find it before you carry on with your own idea.
slides.note: One question, every move: what does that threaten?

slides.title: Review your losses
slides.body: Wins feel good and teach little. In each loss, find the single move where the game turned, and why you missed it.
slides.note: Write the reason in one line. After a few, patterns appear.

slides.title: Play slower games
slides.body: These habits need time. In one-minute games there is none. Rapid gives you room to check every move properly.
slides.note: Play some 15+10 rapid each week, then take the habits back to blitz.

slides.title: Stop after two losses
slides.body: After two losses in a row, the next game is often played angry and fast. That is how a bad hour becomes a bad week.
slides.note: Take a walk. Your rating will still be there.

slides.title: Every plateau is on the poster.
slides.title2: So is the climb after it.
slides.sub: Your whole rating history, on one print.
